content: Implementation Data Level The Implementation Data Level is closer to the actual code implementation in a programming language like C, though it is still an abstraction of the code. Its values correspond to the actual binary numbers handled by the programming lan- guage on the CPU. It contains concepts like pointers and unions which relate to the organization of data in memory and are not relevant for the application level. This level also defines structure, but it can be more granular. For example, the appli- cation level may define a text to be transferred to an instrument cluster as a primitive type (if the structure is not relevant for the application), whereas on the implementation level it could be modeled as an array of bytes.
